## FAQ

What is Mistral Large 4?

It is Mistral AI’s 1 trillion-parameter, natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with a 1M context window. Mistral also calls it “Le Chonk.” The company released its weights publicly on October 29, 2026.

Where can I download Mistral Large 4?

The weights are available on Hugging Face. The model is also available through Mistral’s API for teams that prefer not to host it.

Add as a preferredsource on Google

Infini-AI-Lab has released Hermit, an open-source harness adapter framework for AI agents. Hermit is a framework from Infini-AI-Lab that trains an external ‘harness adapter’ while the agent’s model and harness stay frozen. The first release, v0.1.0, shipped on October 25, 2026. CMU postdoc Haizhong Zheng announced it on X on October 27.

Mistral AI publicly releases Large 4, targets cybersecurity users (https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/mistral-ai-publicly-releases-large-4-targets-cybersecurity-users-2026-10-29/)
【turn38news17】 [wordlim: 100] Published: today; French AI startup Mistral publicly released Large 4 on Thursday, describing it as a model designed to help organisations find and fix cybersecurity vulnerabilities. Unlike systems such as Google Gemini, which are primarily accessed through online services, Large 4 can be downloaded and run independently on an organisation’s own systems, reducing reliance on third-party providers. Mistral said the public version improves on the model unveiled three weeks earlier, following testing with government and corporate users. The company called it its most capable openly available model for cybersecurity, in a field dominated by Chinese AI models. Mistral Vice President of Science Pierre Stock defended the availability of open-weight models, saying he was uncomfortable with a world without them. He noted that once released, access cannot be contained: this can protect users from being cut off, but also allows anyone to use the model.

Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon AI model with cybersecurity focus (https://www.reuters.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-carbon-ai-model-with-cybersecurity-focus-2026-10-28/)
【turn38news18】 [wordlim: 100] Published: yesterday; Google unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model, on Wednesday, intensifying competition with OpenAI and Anthropic in the development of advanced coding and cybersecurity systems. The launch follows the introduction of Gemini 4 Argon two weeks earlier, as Google continues expanding its Gemini model family for developers and enterprise customers. The report identifies cybersecurity as a focus for Carbon but provides no further details about the model’s capabilities or availability.

Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a 'significant leap' in cybersecurity (https://www.theverge.com/tech/1021339/google-gemini-4-carbon-cybersecurity-frontier)
【turn38news19】 [wordlim: 100] Published: today; Google has launched Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier AI model that it says significantly improves coding, agentic work, and cybersecurity over Gemini 4 Argon. Carbon currently leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0, as well as SEC-bench Pro for finding real-world software bugs and ExploitGym for turning vulnerabilities into exploits. Google says the model is designed to handle long, complex engineering tasks, sometimes running for days, and is better at avoiding shortcuts, resisting prompt-injection attacks, and collaborating with users. It also makes half as many unsupported claims as Argon, according to the company. Access is initially limited to selected cybersecurity defense companies, with broader availability planned through Google’s Fairwind Program. Gemini 4 Carbon will launch at Argon’s introductory rates: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

Anthropic unveils additional Claude tools for lawyers (https://www.reuters.com/legal/legalindustry/anthropic-unveils-additional-claude-tools-lawyers-2026-10-28/)
【turn38news20】 [wordlim: 100] Published: yesterday; Anthropic has introduced new “artifacts” for Claude for Legal, responding to lawyers’ requests for more collaborative and customizable tools beyond a standard chatbot. The interactive, visual tools target common legal workflows, including citation checking, regulatory mapping and comparing legal topics. Examples include an Obligations Checker developed with Foley & Lardner and an AI Governance Benchmark created with Goodwin. Users can modify the interface, while artifacts retain the permissions and safeguards already set by their organizations. Anthropic says its legal team uses them for cross-department work on contracts, privacy impact assessments and patents. The launch comes as AI companies compete to serve legal professionals: Google, Thomson Reuters and Microsoft have recently expanded or introduced legal-focused AI products. Anthropic also announced a program to help law schools and public-interest organizations build artifacts for access-to-justice efforts, aiming to broaden access to the technology.
